correctness.rationale: For n≥3 the connected tubes of C_n include n tubes of every proper size 1..n−1 and one full tube, so W_n=Σ_T Δ_T lies in Σx_i=n(n−1)+1. A proper k-tube is a path; exactly k(k+1)/2 sub-tubes lie inside, hence its facet is x(S)=k(k+1)/2. Intrinsic normal in 1^⊥ is 1_S−(k/n)1, squared norm k(n−k)/n, and cyclic symmetry forces vertex barycenter b=(n−1+1/n)1. Its distance to a k-tube facet is [k(n−1+1/n)−k(k+1)/2]/sqrt(k(n−k)/n). Symbolic expansion and fresh exact Fraction replay n=3..200 verify the submitted identity d_k²−d_1²= (k−1)[n(n−k)²+(2n²−7n+4)(n−k)+(n−2)²(n−1)]/[4(n−k)], which is strictly positive for all k≥2 because every bracket contribution is positive/nonnegative for n≥3. The n singleton inequalities x_i≥1 sum to a sharp inradius upper bound r=(n−1)^(3/2)/sqrt(n); equality forces every center coordinate b_i, proving uniqueness and only singleton-facet tangencies. Finite checks corroborate the all-n proof, not the reverse.
